sample_size.excerpt: This was a secondary analysis of the randomized, placebo controlled SELECT (Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial), which included 34,887 men randomly assigned to 4 groups (selenium, vitamin E, selenium plus vitamin E and placebo) in double-blind fashion between August 22, 2001 and June 24, 2004.

cases.excerpt: During a median followup of 7.1 years (IQR 6.4-8.0) 224 bladder cancer cases were recorded.

effect_size.excerpt: There was no significant difference in the bladder cancer incidence between the 53 men in the placebo group and the 56 in the vitamin E group (HR 1.05, IQR 0.64-1.73, p=0.79), the 60 in the selenium group (HR 1.13, 0.70-1.84, p=0.52) or the 55 in the vitamin E plus selenium group (HR 1.05, 0.63-1.70, p=0.86).

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.85–0.96), suggesting that Vitamin E is associated with a lower risk of bladder cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
